question:
What general practices should developers follow when writing code so that attackers cannot exploit it?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Developers should follow secure coding practices to prevent attackers from exploiting software vulnerabilities. This includes validating input, minimizing privileges, sanitizing data, handling errors properly, managing dependencies, using defensive programming, and employing quality assurance techniques throughout the development lifecycle.

# Guidelines

- Validate all input to ensure unexpected or malicious data cannot compromise the system. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Top 10 Software Security Practices.md)
- Adhere to the principle of least privilege, ensuring modules are as small as possible and perform only tasks that require elevated privileges. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Sanitize data sent to other software to prevent injection and related attacks. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Best Practices for Software Development.md)
- Heed compiler warnings, keep designs simple, and default to deny access. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Best Practices and Design Principles.md)
- Practice defense in depth and use effective quality assurance techniques. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Software Security Best Practices.md)
- Ensure program assumptions are validated; if not possible, document them so maintainers know what attackers may try to exploit. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Check every function's error status and [SWEBOK excerpt 6592851bb3f5c8ce07ca]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Prevent code-level security breaches such as buffer overflows or array index bounds violations. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Software Coding and Construction Testing Practices.md)
- Use defensive programming to protect routines from invalid inputs, including checking values of all input parameters. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Contract Design and Error Handling Strategies/Design by Contract and Defensive Programming.md)
- Use automated static code analysis tools [SWEBOK excerpt a6bac0e5d1a7f169fd5a]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Security Testing and Vulnerability Detection/Vulnerability Detection and Analysis Tools/Vulnerability Management and Security Tools.md)
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies and prevent introduction of untrusted external dependencies to reduce vulnerability propagation. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Methods and Languages/Dependency Management and Construction Practices/Managing Software Dependencies and Supply Chain Risks.md)
- Know and reference common vulnerability databases (CVE, CWE, CAPEC) to guide secure implementation. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Security Testing and Vulnerability Detection/Vulnerability Detection and Analysis Tools/Vulnerability Management and Security Tools.md)
- Choose programming languages carefully, as the choice [SWEBOK excerpt bee614598732f0777be8]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Methods and Languages/Programming Language Notation and Security Implications/Programming Language Notations and Security Considerations.md)
- Ensure [SWEBOK excerpt 3919547c5fd6087bd382]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Use inspections, technical reviews including security-oriented reviews, and static analysis as construction quality activities to catch security weaknesses. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Construction Quality Techniques and Practices.md)
- Design exception-handling policies carefully, including all relevant information in exception messages and avoiding empty catch blocks. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Contract Design and Error Handling Strategies/Error Handling, Exception Handling, and Fault Tolerance.md)
- Build security into software engineering from the start rather than treating it as an afterthought, using a Secure Development Life Cycle approach. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Integration and Evaluation Standards/Security Engineering and Secure Development Life Cycle.md)
